front.title: Scenario-Based Service Discovery and Authorization Protocol in Agent Environments

abstract.t:
AI agents act on behalf of end users across applications the agent has no prior relationship with and cannot pre-register with. This specification defines a scenario-based service discovery and authorization protocol for agent environments, which lets an application advertise its capabilities to agents, lets an agent learn how to invoke the application, with which authorization mechanism, and how to obtain a delegated session for the end user without ever handling the end user's primary credentials, and lets the application enforce runtime interaction boundaries when an agent operation exceeds what was approved.
The protocol combines two building blocks. The first is a semantic standard for an application's scenario-based capability advertisement: the scenaric flows the application opens to agents, the operations each flow packages, and the authorization mechanisms and invocation surfaces it accepts for them; what no flow opens is closed by default. The second is an attach and binding standard that attaches the semantic to both mobile applications and web applications, so one advertisement reaches an agent over a web origin or through a packaged native application. The protocol reuses OAuth standards that exist or are being defined and defines no new authorization protocol: the advertisement is a standalone document at its own well-known location, linked from Protected Resource Metadata; the delegated session is established by the grants the advertisement names; tokens are sender-constrained with DPoP; runtime boundaries are carried by Rich Authorization Requests and verified by the authorization schemas framework, whose reverse-guided refusals route the agent back to re-establishment.
